h1: The 5 Best Color Laser Printers and Laser Alternatives for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Color Laser Printers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the one true color laser we found for home offices plus four ink tank and inkjet alternatives, with advice on running costs.
mainKeyword: color laser printer for home office
summary: The Canon MF753Cdw II is the only genuine color laser in our pool, and it is the top pick for steady color printing. The Epson EcoTank ET-4950 is the closest alternative for low running costs, the ET-4800 is the wired-network option, and the Brother and HP inkjets are the cheaper compromises.
intro: Search results for color laser printers are full of inkjets with laser-sounding names. A true color laser uses four toner cartridges and a drum, and its big selling point is that it does not dry out when you print rarely.

We ranked five printers and were upfront about it: only one of them, the Canon, is an actual color laser. The other four are ink tank or cartridge inkjets that serve the same home-office role, so each is labeled for what it is. Our order comes from the spec sheets and what owners report, covering engine type, speed, running cost approach, paper handling and price range.

products.name: Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II Wireless Duplex Laser Printer
products.verdict: The only true four-toner color laser in this ranking.
products.description:
The MF753Cdw II uses a true four-toner color laser engine rated at 35 pages per minute, with wireless duplex, scanner, copier, fax and a document feeder. It carries a three-year limited warranty and costs $200 to $500.

It ranks first by default and by merit, because it is the one printer here that actually matches the title and it will not clog if left idle for weeks. The alternatives below trade that reliability for lower running costs.

Choose it for color documents at real volume. The caveat is a hefty footprint and higher toner costs than a tank system.
products.idealFor: Color documents printed at real volume.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest per-page cost.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4950 Wireless All-in-One Color Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Not a laser, but up to three years of ink is included.
products.description:
The ET-4950 is a color ink-tank printer rather than a laser. It lists up to three years of ink in the box, an 18 ppm print speed, a 2.4 inch color touchscreen and an automatic document feeder. It falls in the $200 to $500 range.

It places second because the bundled ink changes the running-cost picture, which is the main reason people shop for a laser in the first place. Compared with the Canon, you give up speed and the laser engine.

Pick it for a mix of photos and documents. The caveat is that it is not a laser, and tank printers still need occasional use to avoid clogs.
products.idealFor: Mixed color photos and documents on a low running cost.
products.skipIf: You must have a true laser engine.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless All-in-One Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A cheaper tank printer with an Ethernet port.
products.description:
The ET-4800 is a color ink-tank engine with an Ethernet port as well as wireless, a scanner, copier, fax and feeder, and cartridge-free bottle refills. It falls in the $100 to $200 range and costs less than the ET-4950.

It ranks third because it gives up the bundled ink and touchscreen of its sibling, though the price drop is meaningful. The Ethernet jack suits an office with a wired network.

Choose it for a stable wired connection without cartridges. The caveat is that it is also not a laser.
products.skipIf: You want a laser or bundled ink.

products.name: Brother INKvestment MFC-J4555DW Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One
products.verdict: Two paper trays for letterhead and plain paper side by side.
products.description:
A cartridge-based color inkjet, not a laser, with a 2.7 inch touchscreen, two paper trays and higher-capacity INKvestment cartridges. A Refresh Subscription trial is included. Price runs $200 to $500.

It ranks fourth because the two trays are a real convenience for letterhead, but the price matches the Epson tank models, which do more on running costs.

Buy it if you switch between letterhead and plain paper. The caveat is that cartridges cost more per page than tanks.
products.idealFor: Offices loading letterhead and plain paper separately.
products.skipIf: Running cost is your top concern.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The cheapest realistic way into color home-office printing.
products.description:
A standard cartridge color inkjet with an automatic document feeder, duplex printing, a three-month Instant Ink trial, AI-capable setup and a compact all-in-one body. It falls in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks last because it is the least laser-like pick and the cartridge approach carries the highest running cost. What it offers is a low entry price with duplex and a feeder.

Choose it if you print color only now and then. The caveat is that cartridges can dry if the printer sits idle.
products.idealFor: Occasional color printing on a budget.
products.skipIf: You print rarely and need ink that never dries.

whatMatters.detail: Lasers fuse toner onto paper with heat and do not dry out when idle. Inkjets spray liquid that can clog. Check the title for the word laser and the number of toner cartridges.
Pages per minute is how fast pages emerge after the first. 35 ppm suits volume and 18 ppm suits light use. Look for the ppm figure.
Toner, cartridges and tank bottles all have different costs per page. Tank printers tend to cost least over time. Look at what ink is included.
A second tray lets you keep letterhead loaded. It saves swapping paper. Search for the tray count.
A longer warranty reduces risk on a printer you depend on. Check the warranty length in the specs.

faq.a: No. Only the Canon MF753Cdw II is a true color laser. The others are ink tank or cartridge inkjets.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake buying a color laser?
faq.a: Trusting product names. Many inkjets use words like OfficeJet, so check for toner.

faq.q: Is a laser worth it over a tank printer?
faq.a: If you print color daily, yes, for speed and idle reliability. For occasional use, a tank can cost less.
The Canon and HP OfficeJet list duplex. Check the others on their pages.

faq.q: How do I keep inkjets from clogging?
faq.a: Print something every week or two. Idle cartridges and nozzles tend to dry.

faq.q: Is the Instant Ink trial free?
faq.a: The HP lists a three-month trial. Read the enrollment terms before continuing.

finalTake: If you want a real color laser, the Canon MF753Cdw II is the one to buy, because it is the only genuine option in our pool. If running cost matters more, the Epson EcoTank ET-4950 is the best alternative. The ET-4800 adds Ethernet for less.
